title: Gangguan Keseimbangan
subtitle: Kimi rerun: neuro_vestibular
summary: Kuliah komprehensif tentang gangguan keseimbangan yang mencakup anatomi sistem keseimbangan (vestibular, visual, proprioseptif), patofisiologi vertigo dan ketidakseimbangan, pendekatan klinis (anamnesis, pemeriksaan termasuk Romberg, Fukuda, Unterberger, analisis jalan), tes diagnostik (audiometri, VNG, tes kalorik, posturografi), serta kondisi umum termasuk BPPV, penyakit Meniere, neuritis vestibular, neuroma akustik, vestibulopati bilateral, dan PPPD (Persistent Postural-Perceptual Dizziness).

sections.title: Anatomi Sistem Keseimbangan

content.text: Balance is maintained by integration of three sensory systems: VESTIBULAR SYSTEM (inner ear - semicircular canals for angular acceleration, otolith organs for linear acceleration/gravity); VISUAL SYSTEM (provides spatial orientation and reference); and PROPRIoCEPTIVE/SOMATOSENSORY SYSTEM (joint position sense, muscle spindle input from feet and legs). These inputs are integrated in the CEREBELLUM and BRAINSTEM vestibular nuclei, with output to oculomotor system (VOR) and postural muscles. Dysfunction in any system or the integrator can cause imbalance.
Sistem vestibular: kanal semisirkular, organ otolit
Sistem proprioseptif: posisi sendi, sensor kaki
Integrasi: serebelum, nukleus vestibular batang otak

sections.title: Pendekatan Klinis

content.text: HISTORY: Characterize the dizziness (spinning vs lightheaded vs imbalance), duration (seconds/minutes/hours/days), triggers (position change, head movement, standing), associated symptoms (hearing loss, tinnitus, nausea, neurological symptoms), and medical history (hypertension, diabetes, medications). KEY QUESTIONS: Is it true vertigo or non-vertiginous dizziness? Is it constant or episodic? What triggers it? Are there auditory symptoms? Are there neurological symptoms?
Karakter: vertigo vs pusing vs tidak stabil
Pemicu: perubahan posisi, gerakan kepala, berdiri
Gejala penyerta: gangguan dengar, tinitus, mual, defisit neurologis

sections.title: Pemeriksaan Fisik

content.text: ROMBERG TEST: Stand feet together, eyes closed; positive if sway/fall increases with eyes closed (indicates proprioceptive or vestibular loss). SHARPENED ROMBERG: Tandem stance (heel-to-toe), eyes closed. FUKUDA STEPPING TEST: March in place with eyes closed for 50 steps; rotation >30 degrees or forward/backward displacement >50cm suggests unilateral vestibular hypofunction. UNTERBERGER TEST: March in place with eyes closed and arms raised; rotation toward affected side indicates unilateral vestibular lesion. HEAD IMPULSE TEST: Rapid head turn while fixating; catch-up saccade indicates reduced VOR on that side. DIX-HALLPIKE: For BPPV diagnosis - head hanging precipitates rotatory nystagmus. GAIT EXAMINATION: Observe initiation, stride, arm swing, turning, tandem walking.

sections.title: Pemeriksaan Penunjang

content.text: AUDIOGRAM: Pure tone audiometry, speech audiometry, tympanometry. Sensorineural hearing loss with low-frequency component suggests Meniere; asymmetric hearing loss suggests acoustic neuroma. VNG (VIDEO NYSTAGMOGRAPHY): Records eye movements to assess vestibular function. Includes spontaneous nystagmus, gaze testing, smooth pursuit, saccades, optokinetic nystagmus, positional testing, and caloric testing. CALORIC TEST: Gold standard for assessing individual horizontal semicircular canal function. Warm (44C) and cool (30C) water irrigation. Normal response: nystagmus toward irrigated ear with warm, away with cool. Canal paresis: reduced response on one side. Directional preponderance: stronger response in one direction. POSTUROGRAPHY: Computerized platform measuring postural sway under various conditions (eyes open/closed, platform stable/moving).
Audiogram: SNHL low-freq = Meniere; asimetris = neuroma akustik
VNG: nistagmus spontan, smooth pursuit, saccade, kalorik
Tes kalorik: standar emas fungsi kanal horizontal

sections.title: Gangguan Umum dan Manajemen

content.text: BPPV: Epley maneuver for posterior canal; Brandt-Daroff exercises; rare cases require surgery. MENIERE: Low-salt diet, diuretics, betahistine; intratympanic gentamicin or steroids for refractory; endolymphatic sac surgery. VESTIBULAR NEURITIS: Corticosteroids (methylprednisolone) within 72 hours, antiemetics, early vestibular rehabilitation. ACOUSTIC NEUROMA (Vestibular Schwannoma): MRI with contrast; management options include observation, stereotactic radiosurgery, or microsurgical removal depending on size and symptoms. BILATERAL VESTIBULOPATHY: From ototoxic drugs (aminoglycosides), meningitis, autoimmune disorders; vestibular rehabilitation is mainstay. PPPD (Persistent Postural-Perceptual Dizziness): Chronic non-spinning dizziness >3 months, worse with upright posture and complex visual stimuli; treated with SSRIs (sertraline), CBT, and desensitization exercises.
